draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Ponmudi! The road up has 22 hairpin bends, climbing to about 1,100 metres. Ponmudi means 'golden peak', and on clear evenings you'll see why.
draft.hungryLine: Food up here is limited. Grab tea and snacks, and eat properly on the way back.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Stop at the bends for the views, then walk the top of the hill and the deer park.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit on the grassy top and watch the clouds roll up the valley.
moodReplies.surprise-me: On a clear day, you can see Agasthyarkoodam, a peak sacred to the sage Agastya.

legends.title: The sage's mountain
legends.body: The peak is said to be where the sage Agastya meditated. The forest around it is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

legends.title: Count them on the way up
legends.body: There are 22 hairpin bends on the road up. Kids in the car usually count every one.

tips.title: Go up early.
tips.body: Mist often covers the top by afternoon.

tips.title: Check road access.
tips.body: The road can close after heavy rain.

story.title: Forest hills
story.body: These hills are part of the Western Ghats, one of the world's richest forests.

story.title: Tea on the slopes
story.body: Planters grew tea on the lower slopes.

story.title: A cool escape
story.body: People from Thiruvananthapuram started coming up to escape the heat.

story.title: A protected forest
story.body: The Agasthyamala forests were recognised by UNESCO as a biosphere reserve.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Count the bends, walk the top, then head down for a meal. Tell me if the peak lived up to its name.

food.name: Tea stalls at the hilltop
